refresh_policy.rationale: Apple does not publish a rate limit for the CloudKit web service or the icloud.com sign-in surface. This connector is session-reuse-only: it never automates Apple ID sign-in or any two-factor challenge, so a scheduled run either reuses the seeded profile's live session or hands off to the owner via manual_action. First login from a new browser profile commonly serves a two-factor prompt and sometimes a 'Trust this browser?' step, but the session persists in the profile afterward, so most scheduled refreshes reuse it without any prompt. A conservative 12-hour cadence avoids repeatedly exercising Apple's undocumented sign-in friction; assisted_after_owner_auth:true lets a background run ask the owner for bounded help when the session has gone stale.

streams.name: profile
streams.description: The signed-in iCloud account from the existing session validate response. The optional user_name is dsInfo.fullName, omitted when absent or unreadable; no additional network request or inferred fallback is used.

display.label: Your iCloud account
display.detail: Account identity and source-stated display name.

id.description: The signed-in account's dsInfo.dsid from session validation.

user_name.description: Source-stated dsInfo.fullName, omitted when absent or unreadable.

streams.name: notes
streams.description: Notes in iCloud Notes, queried from the CloudKit private database's 'recents' search index. The legacy folder-name projection depends on the folders stream; collection fetches that dependency even when only notes are requested.

display.label: Your iCloud notes
display.detail: Note title, snippet, best-effort extracted body text, pin state, folder name and assignment, attachment flag, and created/modified timestamps.

folder_name.description: Folder display name from the same folder snapshot; null when there is no folder reference or the referenced folder could not be resolved. Unresolved names are reported in the stream omission details and do not count as covered.

is_pinned.description: Whether the note is pinned, or null when CloudKit's flag could not be read. Unreadable fields are named in the stream omission gap and do not count as covered.

has_attachments.description: Whether attachments exist, or null when CloudKit's attachment field could not be read. Unreadable fields are named in the stream omission gap and do not count as covered.

streams.name: folders
streams.description: Folders used to organize iCloud Notes, queried from the CloudKit private database's 'parentless' search index.

display.label: Your iCloud notes folders
display.detail: Folder name and CloudKit record identity.

name.description: Folder title, recordName fallback for a valid empty title, or null when the title field could not be read. Unreadable fields are named in the stream omission gap and do not count as covered.

reason_display_messages.icloud_auth_failed: iCloud Notes did not authorize this query. Check the session and retry.
reason_display_messages.icloud_http_error: iCloud Notes returned an HTTP error. This stream was not marked complete.
reason_display_messages.icloud_invalid_query_response: iCloud Notes returned an unreadable response. This stream was not marked complete.
reason_display_messages.icloud_no_progress: iCloud Notes pagination stopped. This stream was not marked complete.
reason_display_messages.icloud_omitted_rows: Some iCloud Notes fields could not be read or stored. The affected rows are listed in the stream omission details, and the stream was not marked complete.
reason_display_messages.icloud_rate_limited: iCloud Notes temporarily limited requests. Retry collection later.
reason_display_messages.icloud_navigation_changed: The iCloud Notes page changed during collection. This stream was not marked complete.
reason_display_messages.icloud_readiness_exhausted: The iCloud Notes page did not become ready within the retry budget. Collection did not start; retry when the Notes page is available.
